modes.name: user_claim_not_reconciled
modes.definition: The reply presents a user-supplied detail (product, store, date) as a verified order fact without a tool confirming it, or proceeds without stating a conflict between the user's claim and the tool record. This includes dismissing a user's doubt about a record without checking it (support-0045, where the record itself was wrong).
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the detail came from a tool result (e.g. product name confirmed by search_products). Differs from write_on_unconfirmed_target: there the user gave no identifying detail and the agent guessed.
modes.product_change: Rule: reconcile user claims with tool data; label unverified details as user-reported; state conflicts before acting.

modes.name: write_on_unconfirmed_target
modes.definition: The agent performs a write action (refund, cancel) on an order or amount it chose itself when the user did not identify it and the lookups did not narrow it to exactly one candidate.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the user named the order (support-0087) or the agent listed candidates and asked (support-0030). Differs from user_claim_not_reconciled: here nothing the user said conflicted with the record.
modes.product_change: Rule: before a write, ask if the target order or amount is not pinned to one candidate; do not add unstated details.

modes.name: permission_denied_escalated_without_confirming
modes.definition: After a tool returns permission_denied for an order the user named, the agent opens a ticket requesting action on that order without first telling the user and asking them to confirm the order number.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the agent refuses without revealing details and escalates only after the user confirms or insists (support-0046). Differs from duplicate_ticket: the problem is the first ticket, not a repeat.
modes.product_change: Rule: after permission_denied, say the order can't be accessed and ask to confirm the number before escalating.

modes.name: invented_date_reasoning
modes.definition: The agent states or relies on how much time has passed (window passed, overdue, outside window) without a dated source for today, and the claim is false or drives a decision.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the agent relies on refund_eligible without a date claim (support-0034); an unsourced but correct, inconsequential date remark (support-0066) is a boundary case to decide. Differs from ineligible_refund_mishandled: that mode is about the refusal and escalation, this one about date claims.

modes.name: duplicate_ticket
modes.definition: The agent opens a new support ticket, or presents an existing one as a separate issue, when a ticket for the same issue is already open in the conversation and the user added no new issue.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the agent refers to the existing ticket (support-0201, support-0205 turn 3). Differs from refusal_mishandled: that is about whether the first ticket should exist.
modes.product_change: Rule: reuse or reference an open ticket for the same issue; open a new one only for a new issue.

modes.name: out_of_scope_escalated
modes.definition: For a request outside Cartwheel support (e.g. legal advice), the agent opens a support ticket or calls tools instead of declining in one or two sentences and saying what it can help with.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the agent declines without tools (support-0018, support-0174, support-0183). Differs from refusal_mishandled: that covers requests Cartwheel handles but the rules forbid (not eligible, shipped, no permission); this one is the SCOPE-2 rule for requests outside Cartwheel support.
modes.product_change: Rule: out-of-scope requests are declined in one or two sentences with no tool calls.

modes.name: refusal_mishandled
modes.definition:
The rules prohibit what the user was asking for — the refund wasn’t eligible, the order had already shipped, or the system didn’t have permission to access it. 
But the agent didn’t give a clear refusal with the correct governing rule and the next step.
 Instead, it sometimes opened a ticket or suggested an “exception” that no policy supports.
 This includes treating refund_eligible: false as an “automatic” failure, citing the wrong return window (as in support‑0091), and escalating after a permission_denied result without first asking the user to confirm the order number.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the agent refuses and explains the governing rule with a citation (support-0034), or refuses after permission_denied and asks to double-check the number (support-0236, support-0238). A ticket is fine when an ESC rule lists the case, the user reports something to investigate (support-0024, misrouting) or confirms after being asked (support-0046). An accurate refusal that omits the reason, especially when the user asked for brevity, is a boundary case (support-0025). Differs from invented_date_reasoning: a correct refusal can still invent a date, and vice versa. Differs from out_of_scope_escalated: that is about requests outside Cartwheel support.
modes.spec_ref: RESP-5, ESC rules, AUTH-1, cw-cancellations + pending revision #4 and the refund_eligible false revision
modes.product_change: Refusal rule: when a tool or record says no, say so, give the governing rule (store or platform window, shipped status, no access) and the next step; open a ticket only when an ESC rule lists the case; after permission_denied, ask the user to confirm the order number first.

modes.name: inconsistent_record_not_flagged
modes.definition: When a tool record contradicts itself or another record — for example, showing an item shipped after it was delivered or listing a product from a different store — the agent must treat that as an inconsistency. The correct response is to point out the contradiction, avoid asserting any timeline, and escalate. Instead, the agent handled the record as if everything were normal.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when a field is missing and the agent says so without computing from it (support-0028, support-0209: no delivery date). Differs from user_claim_not_reconciled: there a user's claim conflicts with the record; here the record is inconsistent by itself. support-0045 (store mismatch the user doubted) stays in user_claim_not_reconciled; revisit in Part D.
modes.product_change: Rule: before using an order record, check that its dates are in order and its store matches the product; if not, state the inconsistency, do not assert a timeline, and escalate.
